Next steps: can we restore every saturated pixel in the W51 images?¶

2026-10-26

The story in one paragraph. We listed every saturated pixel in all 480 W51 exposures (400 NIRCam, 80 MIRI): 14.7 million pixels. Most of them (78%) already have a value from the pipeline, because they saturated only after one or more good reads. The pixels that really need restoring are the ones saturated already in their first group (level 0): 2.65 million. Of those, 90% sit in huge saturated patches of bright extended emission (mostly MIRI F2100W and F1280W), which are not stars, and our star-trained model cannot restore them; another 6% are bad pixels, hot pixels and cosmic rays. The rest, about 119,000 pixels in star-like regions, all get a value. For NIRCam, 90% of them get a value we can trust (from the first read, or from the model where it is confident); for MIRI only 15% do. Sample restored images are in section 4. Section 5 lists what to do next, in order.

Words used here¶

word meaning
level 0 a pixel saturated already in its first group: the pipeline has no value for it
level 1-4 saturated later: the pipeline measured it from its unsaturated groups
region a connected patch of saturated pixels (usually one star)
huge region a patch of more than 10,000 connected saturated pixels: bright extended emission, not a star
first read the detector's first read (NIRCam ZEROFRAME), which measures many level-0 pixels directly
training-quality star a region fitted by the PSF fit whose labels passed all cuts: the model learned from such stars
never fitted a star-like region the PSF fit skipped (wings missing, fit failed, ...): no label to check against
trusted the model's own 16-84% uncertainty is narrower than 0.3 dex (a factor 2)
dex a factor on a log scale: 0.1 dex = x1.26, 0.3 dex = x2

1. Where we stand¶

From report_v5_20261025.ipynb: the v5 labels use the first reads, the line + trees model is nearly unbiased on the fair brightness test (NIRCam level 0: within 0.05 dex up to 32x beyond its training stars, scatter 0.09-0.29 dex), and MIRI is weaker (scatter 0.26-0.38 dex, biased low beyond x8). Four questions from that report are still open for you (repeated in section 6).

The model was trained on stars. This notebook asks the practical question: when we run it on the real W51 images, which saturated pixels can it restore, and how well? To answer it, py/restore_image.py (new) was run on all 480 exposures. For every saturated pixel it records how the pixel is restored:

method which pixels
pipeline value level 1-4 pixels with a value from their unsaturated groups: kept as they are
first read NIRCam level-0 pixels whose first read is below saturation and that do not touch a fully saturated (A-hard) pixel
model the other pixels of star-like regions (A-hard pixels and their touching ring, MIRI level 0, and level 1-4 pixels without a pipeline value)
no restoration huge regions (extended emission), bad pixels, MIRI pixels outside the science area

The model needs nothing from the PSF fit, so it can run on any region; whether its answer is right is the question of sections 3 and 4.

2. Every saturated pixel in W51¶

2.1 Most saturated pixels already have a value¶

Reading it. 14.7 million saturated pixels in total (9.6 M in the 80 MIRI exposures, 5.1 M in the 400 NIRCam exposures). About 78% saturated only after one or more good reads and have a pipeline value (grey). The 2.65 million level-0 pixels (orange) are the ones without any value. A small number of level 1-4 pixels also have no pipeline value (yellow; for example MIRI pixels whose only good read was dropped by the pipeline).

2.2 Where the level-0 pixels are¶

In [3]:
lf = pd.read_csv(f'{C}/tables/level0_filter_category.csv')
lf['kind'] = lf.category.map({'huge region': 'huge region (extended emission)', 'bad pixel': 'bad pixel, 3x3 junk or no data',
                             'junk 3x3': 'bad pixel, 3x3 junk or no data', 'outside science area': 'bad pixel, 3x3 junk or no data',
                             'model': 'star-like region', 'first read': 'star-like region'})
t = lf.groupby(['filter', 'kind']).pixels.sum().unstack().fillna(0)
wl = t.index.str[1:-1].astype(int)
t = t.iloc[np.argsort(wl)]
kinds = [('star-like region', AQUA), ('huge region (extended emission)', GREY), ('bad pixel, 3x3 junk or no data', LIGHT)]
share = t.div(t.sum(axis=1), axis=0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 6.5))
left = np.zeros(len(t))
for k, c in kinds:
    ax.barh(t.index, 100 * share[k], left=left, color=c, edgecolor='white', linewidth=1.5, label=k)
    left += 100 * share[k].values
for i, (f, tot) in enumerate(t.sum(axis=1).items()):
    ax.text(101, i, f'{fmt(tot)} level-0 pixels ({fmt(t.loc[f, "star-like region"])} star-like)', va='center', fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.set_xlim(0, 160); ax.set_xticks([0, 25, 50, 75, 100]); ax.set_xlabel('share of the filter\'s level-0 pixels (%)')
ax.invert_yaxis(); ax.grid(axis='y', visible=False); ax.legend(loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.35, -0.1), ncol=3)
plt.tight_layout()

Reading it.

  • MIRI F2100W, F1280W and F770W: almost all level-0 pixels are in huge saturated patches: the bright extended emission of the W51 HII regions fills the detector's wells over large areas (an example is in section 4). F2100W alone has 1.6 million such pixels.
  • NIRCam short wave (F140M-F210M): about 16,000 level-0 pixels per filter are flagged bad pixels (detector defects flagged as saturated in every exposure) and about 7,300 are 3x3 "junk" (a single hot pixel or cosmic ray, flagged with its 8 neighbours); the star-like level-0 pixels are 750 (F187N) to 9,400 (F182M) per filter.
  • NIRCam long wave: about 5,400 junk pixels per filter, huge regions of extended emission in F360M, F410M and F480M (13,000-30,000 pixels), and 1,300 (F405N) to 11,000 (F360M) star-like pixels.
  • MIRI F560W: nearly all level-0 pixels are star-like.

In total, about 119,000 level-0 pixels are in star-like regions (68,000 NIRCam, 51,000 MIRI): the ones our method is designed for.

2.3 Which of them can be used to train and test the model?¶

A pixel can be used for training and testing only if its star was fitted by the PSF fit and the labels passed all cuts (a "training-quality star").

Reading it. For NIRCam, 82% of the star-like level-0 pixels belong to training-quality stars; for MIRI only 8%. Most MIRI star-like level-0 pixels (41,000 of 51,000) are in regions the PSF fit never fitted. The model has never seen anything like them, and no label exists to check it there.

2.4 Are the never-fitted regions like the training stars?¶

In [5]:
reg = pd.read_parquet(f'{C}/regions.parquet')
reg['dom'] = np.where(reg.status == 'training label', 'training-quality star',
                      np.where(reg.status == 'region not fitted', 'never fitted', np.where(reg.status.str.startswith('fitted'), 'fitted, labels cut', 'other')))
reg = reg[(reg.dom != 'other') & (reg.n_level0 > 0)]
bins = np.logspace(0, 4, 33)
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4.6), sharey=False)
for ax, inst in zip(axes, ['NIRCam', 'MIRI']):
    for dom, c, ls in [('training-quality star', AQUA, '-'), ('fitted, labels cut', GREY, '--'), ('never fitted', ORANGE, '-')]:
        h = reg[(reg.inst == inst) & (reg.dom == dom)]
        ax.hist(h.sat_area, bins=bins, histtype='step', color=c, lw=2, ls=ls, label=f'{dom} ({len(h):,} regions)')
    ax.set_xscale('log'); ax.set_xlabel('saturated area of the region (pixels)'); ax.set_title(f'{inst}: regions with level-0 pixels')
    ax.legend(fontsize=9.5)
axes[0].set_ylabel('regions')
plt.tight_layout()

Reading it. Training-quality stars have saturated areas of a few to a few hundred pixels. The never-fitted regions with level-0 pixels reach thousands of pixels (MIRI especially): very bright stars merged with nebulosity, or patches of extended emission just below the 10,000-pixel "huge" limit. The model would have to extrapolate far for those.

3. Can we restore them, and how well?¶

3.1 A physical check that needs no label¶

Inside one region, a pixel that saturated in its first group filled faster than the pixels that saturated in the second group. So a restored level-0 pixel should be at least about as bright as the region's level-1 pixels (which have pipeline values). A restored level-0 value below 0.8x their median is physically implausible.

In [6]:
oc = pd.read_csv(f'{C}/tables/order_check.csv')
oc = oc[oc.level0]
doms = ['training-quality star', 'fitted, cut', 'never fitted']
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 4.2))
x = np.arange(3)
for k, (inst, c) in enumerate([('NIRCam', BLUE), ('MIRI', ORANGE)]):
    v = oc[oc.inst == inst].set_index('domain').reindex(doms)
    bars = ax.bar(x + (k - 0.5) * 0.38, 100 * v.implausible, width=0.36, color=c, label=inst, edgecolor='white', linewidth=2)
    for b, val, n in zip(bars, v.implausible, v.pixels):
        ax.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width() / 2, 100 * val + 2, f'{100 * val:.0f}%\n({fmt(n)} px)', ha='center', fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
ax.set_xticks(x, doms); ax.set_ylabel('model level-0 values that are implausible (%)'); ax.set_ylim(0, 105)
ax.legend(loc='upper left'); ax.set_title('Model-restored level-0 pixels: below 0.8x the region\'s level-1 pixels')
Out[6]:
Text(0.5, 1.0, "Model-restored level-0 pixels: below 0.8x the region's level-1 pixels")

Reading it. On training-quality stars the model is never implausible in NIRCam and rarely in MIRI (3%). In NIRCam it stays plausible even in never-fitted regions (2.5%). In MIRI never-fitted regions, 84% of the model's level-0 values are implausible: there the model does not work.

3.2 The model knows when it is unsure¶

The model gives a 16-84% range for each pixel. Where its range is narrower than 0.3 dex (a factor 2), we call it "trusted". Does that catch the failures?

In [7]:
gc = pd.read_csv(f'{C}/tables/gate_check.csv')
gc = gc[gc.gate == 'narrow']
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 4.4))
for ax, inst in zip(axes, ['NIRCam', 'MIRI']):
    v = gc[gc.inst == inst].set_index('domain').reindex(doms)
    x = np.arange(3)
    ax.bar(x - 0.2, 100 * v.kept, width=0.38, color=BLUE, label='trusted (kept)', edgecolor='white', linewidth=2)
    ax.bar(x + 0.2, 100 * v.implausible_rejected.fillna(0), width=0.38, color=ORANGE, label='implausible among the rejected', edgecolor='white', linewidth=2)
    for i, (k_, r_) in enumerate(zip(v.kept, v.implausible_rejected)):
        ax.text(i - 0.2, 100 * k_ + 2, f'{100 * k_:.0f}%', ha='center', fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
        if np.isfinite(r_):
            ax.text(i + 0.2, 100 * r_ + 2, f'{100 * r_:.0f}%', ha='center', fontsize=9.5, color=INK)
    ax.set_xticks(x, doms, fontsize=9.5); ax.set_ylim(0, 110); ax.set_title(inst)
axes[0].set_ylabel('% of model level-0 pixels'); axes[0].legend(loc='upper right', fontsize=9.5)
plt.tight_layout()

Reading it. The uncertainty gate keeps 90-100% of the pixels of training-quality stars and rejects 99% of the MIRI never-fitted pixels, 85% of which were implausible. So the model's own uncertainty is a usable "do not trust me here" flag. (For NIRCam never-fitted regions the gate keeps 66% and those are as plausible as the rest.)

So: we can give a value to every saturated pixel that belongs to a star. For NIRCam 90% of the star-like level-0 pixels get a value we can stand behind; for MIRI only 15%. The huge patches of bright extended emission (90% of all level-0 pixels, nearly all in MIRI) are outside what this approach can do.

In [9]:
SAMPLES = [('F410M', 'jw06151001001_03107_00006_nrcblong'), ('F360M', 'jw06151001001_03105_00005_nrcblong'),
           ('F182M', 'jw06151001001_03105_00006_nrcb4'), ('F2100W', 'jw06151002001_0210j_00001_mirimage'),
           ('F1280W', 'jw06151002002_02107_00003_mirimage'), ('F560W', 'jw06151002001_02101_00004_mirimage')]
METHOD_CLASSES = [('not saturated', 'white'), ('pipeline value', LIGHT), ('first read', AQUA), ('model, trusted', BLUE),
                  ('model, not trusted', YELLOW), ('no restoration', ORANGE)]
cmap_m = ListedColormap([c for _, c in METHOD_CLASSES])
status = pd.read_parquet(f'{C}/pixels.parquet', columns=['file', 'x', 'y', 'status', 'label'],
                         filters=[('file', 'in', [n for _, n in SAMPLES])])

def load(name):
    with fits.open(f'{S}/{name}_cal.fits') as h:
        after, method, err = h['SCI'].data.astype(float), h['RESTORE_METHOD'].data, h['RESTORE_ERR'].data
    cls = method.astype(int).copy()                          # 0 not sat, 1 pipeline, 2 first read, 3 model, 4 none
    cls[cls == 4] = 5
    cls[(method == 3) & ~(err < 0.3)] = 4                     # model, not trusted
    low = np.nanpercentile(after, 1)
    after[(method == 0) & ~np.isfinite(after)] = low         # empty for other reasons (bad pixels, cosmic rays): shown dark
    before = after.copy()
    before[np.isin(method, [2, 3])] = np.nan                 # the pixels that had no value before
    p = pd.read_parquet(glob.glob(f'{S}/*{name}_saturated.parquet')[0])
    p = p.merge(status[status.file == name][['x', 'y', 'status', 'label']], on=['x', 'y'], how='left')
    return before, after, cls, p

def show(ax, img, norm, title):
    cm = plt.get_cmap('gray').copy(); cm.set_bad(ORANGE)
    ax.imshow(img, origin='lower', cmap=cm, norm=norm, interpolation='nearest')
    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_xticks([]); ax.set_yticks([]); ax.grid(False)

def full_frame(filt, name):
    before, after, cls, p = load(name)
    norm = simple_norm(after[np.isfinite(after)], 'asinh', vmin=np.nanpercentile(after, 1), vmax=np.nanpercentile(after, 99.7))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(18, 6.4))
    show(axes[0], before, norm, f'{filt}: before')
    show(axes[1], after, norm, 'after')
    axes[2].imshow(cls, origin='lower', cmap=cmap_m, vmin=-0.5, vmax=5.5, interpolation='nearest')
    axes[2].set_title('how each saturated pixel was restored'); axes[2].set_xticks([]); axes[2].set_yticks([]); axes[2].grid(False)
    counts = pd.Series(cls[cls > 0]).value_counts()
    fig.legend(handles=[Patch(fc=c, ec=GREY, label=f'{n} ({fmt(counts.get(i, 0))})') for i, (n, c) in enumerate(METHOD_CLASSES) if i > 0],
               loc='lower center', ncol=5, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.04))
    plt.tight_layout()
    return before, after, cls, p

def zoom(filt, name, data, region, r=22, title=''):
    before, after, cls, p = data
    g = p[p.region == region]
    w = 1 / (g.sat_level.clip(0) + 1)
    cx, cy = np.average(g.x, weights=w), np.average(g.y, weights=w)
    sl = (slice(max(int(cy) - r, 0), int(cy) + r), slice(max(int(cx) - r, 0), int(cx) + r))
    a = after[sl]
    norm = simple_norm(a[np.isfinite(a)], 'log', vmin=max(np.nanpercentile(a, 2), 1e-3), vmax=np.nanmax(a))
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(19, 4.6))
    show(axes[0], before[sl], norm, 'before'); show(axes[1], a, norm, 'after')
    axes[2].imshow(cls[sl], origin='lower', cmap=cmap_m, vmin=-0.5, vmax=5.5, interpolation='nearest')
    axes[2].set_title('method'); axes[2].set_xticks([]); axes[2].set_yticks([]); axes[2].grid(False)
    rr = np.hypot(g.x - cx, g.y - cy)
    ax = axes[3]
    for m, c, lab in [('pipeline', GREY, 'pipeline value'), ('first read', AQUA, 'first read'), ('model', BLUE, 'model')]:
        s = g.method == m
        ax.scatter(rr[s], g.restored[s], s=10, color=c, label=lab, zorder=2)
    if g.label.notna().any():
        ax.scatter(rr, g.label, s=14, facecolors='none', edgecolors=INK, lw=0.6, label='PSF-fit label', zorder=3)
    ax.set_yscale('log'); ax.set_xlabel('distance from the region centre (px)'); ax.set_ylabel('MJy/sr')
    ax.legend(fontsize=9); ax.set_title('profile')
    fig.suptitle(f'{filt} region {region}: {title}', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold')
    plt.tight_layout()

def regions_by(data, domain_status, r=22):
    # the region with the most model pixels whose cutout lies on the detector (few empty pixels)
    after, p = data[1], data[3]
    m = p[(p.method == 'model') & (p.status == domain_status)]
    for reg in m.groupby('region').size().sort_values(ascending=False).index[:20]:
        g = p[p.region == reg]
        if (g.reason_none == 'bad pixel').any():   # a star on a dead-pixel cluster: not a fair example
            continue
        cx, cy = int(g.x.median()), int(g.y.median())
        cut = after[max(cy - r, 0):cy + r, max(cx - r, 0):cx + r]
        if cut.shape == (2 * r, 2 * r) and np.isnan(cut).mean() < 0.05:
            return [reg]
    return []

Reading the samples.

  • Training-quality stars (NIRCam and MIRI): the restored core continues the star's profile smoothly from the pipeline values outward, and it follows the PSF-fit label. This is the regime the tests in report_v5_20261025.ipynb measure. The innermost core pixels can still be marked "not trusted" (yellow): they are the brightest, fully saturated pixels, where the model's uncertainty is largest.
  • Never-fitted NIRCam regions are usually very bright stars merged with nebulosity; the model's core can be lumpy and scattered (F360M example), and there is nothing to check it against.
  • MIRI never-fitted regions are mostly bright extended emission: the model values there fall below the surrounding pipeline values (implausible, section 3.1) and are flagged "not trusted" (yellow).
  • F2100W: the large orange patch in the map is one huge saturated region of extended emission. It stays a hole.

5. What to do next¶

In order of priority. Items 1-4 make the current restoration safe to use; 5-7 extend it; 8-9 check it independently.

# what why how / effort
1 Gate the model in restore_image.py: use model values only where the 16-84% half-width is < 0.3 dex and the level-0 value passes the saturation-order check; mark the rest "not restored" MIRI never-fitted regions are 84% implausible; the gate keeps 90-100% of training-quality stars a few lines; re-run the census (30 min)
2 Widen the uncertainty band beyond the training range (open decision 2 of report_v5) for brighter stars the band holds 25-46% instead of 68% calibrate the widening on the brightness bands; hours
3 Decide the touching-ring convention (open decision 3): restore the star's light (photon rate) or the recorded charge the two differ by up to x2-3 next to the largest cores your decision; then add the core size as an input to the line; hours
4 Restore small-core rings from the first read (open decision 1) no measurable spill around cores of 1-2 A-hard pixels; direct share 14% to 24% an hour of code; 2-hour v5 re-run
5 More training stars from the never-fitted regions 41,000 MIRI and 6,700 NIRCam star-like level-0 pixels have no label; they are the regions where the model is least reliable read the fit-skip reasons from the v5 logs; relax the wing-coverage rule for crowded fields, or fit pairs of stars together; a day
6 MIRI: test an stpsf PSF broadened per filter for the labels MIRI cores are broader than stpsf; only 255 MIRI training-quality regions a day
7 Extended emission (huge regions): leave them as holes in single exposures, and fill them at the mosaic stage from other dithers or exposures where the same sky is not saturated 2.4 million level-0 pixels; no star model applies check how much of the huge regions every dither saturates (the census has the positions); a day
8 Dither consistency test: the same star saturates differently in different dithers; compare the aperture fluxes of restored stars across dithers an independent check of the restoration without any PSF label restore all exposures of one filter; a day
9 Total-flux test v4 vs v5 (from report_v5) v5 stars at the 80-95th percentile are 9-14% fainter than v4 dithers and narrow-band filters; hours

6. Decisions for you¶

  1. Gate the model with the uncertainty and saturation-order checks (item 1)? Recommended: yes.
  2. Touching ring: light or charge (item 3)? My recommendation: light, so the restored star keeps its total flux.
  3. Small-core rings from the first read (item 4)? Recommended: yes.
  4. Extended emission (item 7): leave as holes in single exposures and fill at the mosaic stage? Recommended.
  5. The order of items 5, 6, 8, 9.
